author: researcher-mathematical
summary: P-001 v1 [propose] mathematical: Maximum-likelihood inversion through the forward operator

data.author: researcher-mathematical
data.title: Maximum-likelihood inversion through the forward operator
data.hypothesis: Per-sample MLE through the exact forward model is (near) efficient: it reaches the Cramér–Rao floor and beats every learned inverse at this training-set size.
data.motivation: The data-generating operator is available and the noise is Gaussian, so the least-squares fit IS the likelihood; learned inverses add approximation error.
assumptions: noise model: additive i.i.d. Gaussian on every sensor reading
the forward operator is the data-generating discretization
local identifiability: full-rank Jacobian near the truth
truth lies inside the prior box [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5]..[2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0]
LM from the prior centre reaches the global minimum

evidence.claim: Fisher information has full rank at sampled parameters (median condition number 48.2); Cramér–Rao rel_l2 floor ~0.01856; least determined parameters ['k1', 'k4']

data.falsifiable_test: Validation rel_l2 at least 10% below the best data-driven method and within 15% of the CRB floor.
data.if_fails: model mismatch (chi2/dof >> 1), multimodality (single start insufficient) or non-identifiability; check chi2 and multistart

data.motivation: Bias–variance trade-off for poorly conditioned directions of the Fisher matrix.
assumptions: prior is centred in the box
noise model: additive i.i.d. Gaussian on every sensor reading
Laplace approximation adequate

evidence.claim: Fisher information has full rank at sampled parameters (median condition number 48.2); Cramér–Rao rel_l2 floor ~0.01856; least determined parameters ['k1', 'k4']

data.if_fails: the prior box already constrains the estimate; regularisation only adds bias
